analysis:
The change is confined to a test file (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift). According to the patch excerpt, the head side edits the comment near line 713 and the pool-lockstep assertions near lines 720-724. It also adds a test at about lines 729-755, `widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry`. The new assertions expect `prefillChunkSize == EngineV2Factory.widePrefillChunkTokens`, `soloPrefillStripeTokens == nil`, and `paged.pool.config.maxPrefillChunk == defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens`. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the new test body past `prepare(...)` was not visible. The base text shows no other logic in the tests that could weaken a production control. No production code changed in the supplied units.

Security-relevant behavior I checked in the base tests, none changed by this diff: the KV-backend kill switch and crash-loop guard degrade explicitly (T-041 sign-off territory), an explicit paged request refuses instead of silently degrading, and the SSD prefix cache is gated by backend and layout. Tests use ephemeral keys, an isolated root and a `/dev/null` guard path, so they touch no real KEK or cache.

Remaining integration questions: the production change that introduces `widePrefillChunkTokens` for Gemma 4 and removes the default solo-prefill stripe is outside these units. A pool whose `maxPrefillChunk` is smaller than the scheduled chunk would hit the `PagedSequenceKV` precondition and abort the process. This is an availability concern (T-010/T-029 class), not visible in this diff. The test asserts the pool stays at the stripe size while `prefillChunkSize` is the wide value. Whether `maxPrefillChunk` still covers the wide plain chunk depends on that unseen production code, which a later pass should confirm. This needs no threat-model update. No findings.
